narrative.intro: National Government Services obligated $278M in federal contract obligations in FY26 to date. National Government Services received 8 awards so far, with an average award size of $34.8M, and obligations were up 6.6% year over year. Historical obligations show variability: FY21 was $256M, FY22 was $254M, FY23 was $285M, FY24 was $186M, FY25 was $261M, and FY26 is $278M. National Government Services concentrates obligations in a few markets. Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers accounted for $204M of obligations, Computer Systems Design Services accounted for $64M, and Other Computer Related Services accounted for $10.3M. The current-year totals are partial because FY26 is fiscal year to date. The page notes that all figures are contract obligations except award-value figures in largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables, which are total contract values. Use the award count and average award size to assess deal scale, and use the market breakdown to identify where most obligations sit.

sections.heading: How has National Government Services' federal spending trended year over year?
sections.body: National Government Services obligated $278M in FY26 to date, which is up 6.6% year over year. National Government Services previously obligated $261M in FY25 and $186M in FY24, with a peak at $285M in FY23. The pattern shows fluctuations across FY21 to FY26 rather than steady growth.

sections.heading: Where do National Government Services' obligations concentrate?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers is the largest market with $204M in obligations. Computer Systems Design Services is the second market with $64M, and Other Computer Related Services accounts for $10.3M. These three markets capture the bulk of reported obligations in FY26 to date.
